title: How do we divide 4500 rupees in the ratio 2 : 3?
description: Four thousand five hundred rupees is divided into two parts in the ratio two to three, the same way as the sharing example in the book. The terms are added to get five groups, one group is found, and each part is its terms times one group.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the terms to get the number of equal groups, find one group, then multiply each term by it. Watch for students who divide the amount by each term separately.

video_script.why: The child divides an amount of money in a given ratio, using the method of the sharing example.
video_script.substitution: Add the terms to get the groups, divide the amount by the groups, then multiply each term by one group.
video_script.anchor: a money card showing four thousand five hundred rupees, ready to be split into two parts
video_script.payoff_line: the two parts are one thousand eight hundred rupees and two thousand seven hundred rupees

final_answer.spoken: one thousand eight hundred rupees and two thousand seven hundred rupees

video_script.design: One idea: terms added give the groups, one group times each term gives the parts. The money card stays in the anchor band and the working goes on the board.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a money card 4500 rupees with a split line and the ratio 2 : 3 under it

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ratio: the ratio 2 : 3 appears under the card
marks.ask: a question mark glows over the split line

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='money'/>It has four thousand five hundred rupees.
<bookmark mark='ratio'/>The money is divided into two parts in the ratio two to three.

beats.on_screen: the money card holds still and the question mark glows

marks.stop: the question mark glows in the accent colour

beats.on_screen: 12 counters in a row split into 4 equal groups of 3, with the ratio 3 : 1 above and the groups 9 and 3 below; the money card slides beside the counters

marks.groups: the counters split into 4 groups of 3
marks.parts: the parts 9 and 3 appear under the groups
marks.same: the money card 4500 slides beside the counters

narration: <bookmark mark='example'/>The example in your book shared twelve counters in the ratio three to one.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Three plus one is four, so there are four equal groups of three.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>One part takes three groups and the other takes one, which makes nine and three.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We will share the money the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Given: amount ₹4500, ratio of the two parts 2 : 3

marks.given: the amount and the ratio are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four thousand five hundred rupees to be divided in the ratio two to three.

marks.find: the thing to find is written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the two parts.
<bookmark mark='groups'/>Step one, add the terms two and three to get five groups.
<bookmark mark='size'/>Divide four thousand five hundred by five, which gives nine hundred rupees in one group.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, multiply each term by one group. The first part is two times nine hundred, which is eighteen hundred.
<bookmark mark='second'/>The second part is three times nine hundred, which is twenty seven hundred.

beats.on_screen: put the answers back: 1800 + 2700 = 4500; 1800 : 2700 = 2 : 3 (divide both by 900)

marks.back: the words put the answers back in the question are written

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step three, put the answers back in the question.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Eighteen hundred plus twenty seven hundred is four thousand five hundred, the whole amount.
<bookmark mark='ratio'/>Divide both parts by nine hundred and we get two to three.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The two parts are one thousand eight hundred rupees and two thousand seven hundred rupees.
